description: Canonical Linux processor capture rule shared by every SDK and by replay-host observation. The same host yields the same sorted capability list from every implementation. A non-Linux host captures nothing. A read or parse failure captures nothing. Capture never removes a captured value, it only maps raw views through these curated tables.
capability_normalization: A curated group name maps to its capability suffix by ASCII lowercasing and mapping '_' to '-'. The inverse mapping uppercases ASCII letters and maps '-' back to '_'.

x86_64.source: The flags line and identity fields of /proc/cpuinfo. The kernel already hides features the operating system did not enable, so the flags line is the process-visible view.

os_enabled_states.osxsave: The cpuinfo flag osxsave is present.
os_enabled_states.xcr0.avx: The cpuinfo flag avx is present. The kernel reports avx only when XCR0 enables the AVX state.
os_enabled_states.xcr0.avx512: The cpuinfo flag avx512f is present. The kernel reports avx512f only when XCR0 enables the AVX-512 state.

arm64.source: AT_HWCAP (key 16) from /proc/self/auxv for feature groups. /proc/cpuinfo identity fields for the identity token.

os_enabled_states.auxv.hwcaps: The auxiliary vector was readable and supplied AT_HWCAP.

identity_rules: Identity field values are ASCII lowercased at capture. The lowercase form is the canonical captured form.

Every identity field value must match ^[a-z0-9-]+$ after lowercasing, except the x86 vendor and microcode and the arm implementer, variant, part, and revision, which may also contain 'x' from a hexadecimal prefix. A value outside this shape omits the identity.
The x86 family, model, and stepping fields must parse as base ten unsigned 32-bit integers.
When /proc/cpuinfo contains more than one processor block, the identity is captured only when every block reports the same identity tuple. Disagreement omits the identity.
A missing field omits the identity. An omitted identity is conservative because static capture may only add information, never fabricate it.
